findings.conclusion: The pinned base has exactly one rank-two readout path, after a later-query pre-assimilation GRU step; rank-three nonquery sequence readouts retain the original output head.

For identical existing parameters and copied output/prior_output tensors, forward arithmetic, correction, capture mapping and carry are unchanged. The two separate readout parameter gradients sum to the shared-head gradient, subject to floating-point accumulation order.

The first later-query prior loss has no decision-head path. An initial nonquery loss has no prior-head path. Both share the backbone, and subsequent nonquery losses can reach the prior head through query correction. No backbone or post-training decision isolation is claimed.

Later-query prior values use the current public features and previous anchor/carry before current query-score assimilation. Exact current-query prediction override and future-input rejection semantics are inherited.

Inherited active-mask validation, unused-score poison tolerance, positive-zero prior padding, first-query exclusion, detached owned carry, ended-lane behavior and finally-based capture cleanup are preserved.

Existing modules are constructed before the additional head, preserving their paired seeded initialization. Both new head tensors are zeroed. make_head preserves caller Torch RNG through the inherited fork pattern. Added parameter counts are 120 for innovation and 116 for innovation_gru.
Six paired-family tests plus four malformed-input cases give 16 authored cases covering byte comparisons, a scalar GRU oracle, gradient routing, causality, carry/chunk behavior and injected failures.

limitations: No component or test imports, model calls, test execution, training, simulator calls or empirical array reads occurred in this review.
This is source consistency review, not runtime qualification, gradient measurement, performance evidence or scientific efficacy evidence.
Rank-based dispatch is valid only for the pinned internal base call contract; callers must authenticate both frozen dependencies.
Equivalence requires copying the old head into the prior head. Independently trained heads can alter corrections and all later recurrent states.
Synthetic gradient nonzero assertions and exact numerical comparisons remain to be established by the separately recorded runtime qualification.
